definitions.explanation: A customer using a shop or service for the first time, as opposed to a repeat customer. Business vocabulary used in marketing and sales talk.

examples.japanese: {新規客|しんききゃく}が{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: The number of new customers is rising.

examples.japanese: {新規客|しんききゃく}には{割引|わりびき}クーポンを{配|くば}っている。
examples.english: We hand out discount coupons to new customers.

examples.japanese: {新規客|しんききゃく}を{集|あつ}めるより、{今|いま}いる{客|きゃく}に{通|かよ}い{続|つづ}けてもらうほうが{費用|ひよう}は{安|やす}い。
examples.english: It costs less to keep existing customers coming back than to attract new ones.

notes:
{新規|しんき} (new, fresh) + {客|きゃく} (customer). Heard constantly in retail and service businesses, where it is contrasted with returning custom.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {新規客|しんききゃく}を{獲得|かくとく}する: to win new customers
- {新規客|しんききゃく}{向|む}けのキャンペーン: a campaign aimed at new customers
- {新規客|しんききゃく}の{開拓|かいたく}: developing new custom

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {常連|じょうれん}: regular customer — someone who comes repeatedly
- {既存客|きぞんきゃく}: existing customer — the term {新規客|しんききゃく} is usually contrasted with in business planning
